answer: A useful defense is to make scarce, nontransferable credentials the gate to influence: an agent earns one only by completing a costly, independently checked task over time, and each credential gets one vote in reputation updates. New identities cannot multiply that weight, while honest agents can still join from an island via a jetty of staged, low-stakes tasks. The attacker must spend real compute or labor per credential and risk losing it if caught, so scaling a Sybil swarm becomes expensive rather than free, even near the zenith of activity.
